rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
rules.requirement: In housing funded by or on land from Boston DND, or with income-restricted units under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy, providers may not use blanket bans on applicants with arrests or convictions. They may not consider non-conviction arrests, expunged or sealed convictions, juvenile records, or convictions over 5 years old, with exceptions for direct relationship or unreasonable risk. Credit scores may not be used to approve or deny applications.
rules.key_value: No blanket criminal-history bans; no convictions older than 5 years; no credit score use
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND, Feb. 2017)
citation_aliases: Boston DND Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
rules.quoted_span: will not impose a blanket policy that denies housing to anyone with arrests and or convictions. Housing providers will consider applicants on a case-by-case basis
rules.effective_date_note: Policy document dated February 2017; exact effective date not stated.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing providers receiving DND funding and/or land, or with income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply where a conviction has a direct relationship to the housing sought or poses unreasonable risk of substantial harm to others, or to current criminal behavior.
rules.interaction: Conflicting federal or state criminal-history requirements preempt this policy.

requires_unknown_facts: property receives City (DND) funding or land, or has income-restricted units under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy

rules.title: Boston fair housing protections (rental assistance / Section 8 vouchers)
rules.requirement: Landlords in Boston may not discriminate against renters based on protected traits, including rental assistance such as Section 8, disability or veterans vouchers. Refusing to accept rental assistance is illegal housing discrimination.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Housing Regulations (Boston Fair Housing Commission)
rules.quoted_span: The landlord tells you they don't accept rental assistance. This includes Section 8 vouchers, social security disability vouchers, and veterans vouchers.
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date.
rules.penalty: Complaints are investigated by the Fair Housing Commission, which tries to resolve them.
rules.review_note: Page cites no code section; cited by the name the page uses.

rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act
rules.requirement: A landlord planning to end a tenancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources at the same time as the notice to quit or non-renewal. The landlord must also send a copy of the notice to the City. A violation draws a warning, then $300 per day, but does not halt the eviction.
rules.key_value: Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources with notice to quit; $300/day fine after a warning
rules.quoted_span: The Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources must be delivered at the same time as the Notice to Quit
rules.effective_date_note: Tenant FAQ states HSNA becomes effective November 6, 2020; ordinance passed October 2020.
rules.exemptions: Residences in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities, and non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities. Requirements cannot be waived.
rules.penalty: 1st offense: warning; 2nd and subsequent offenses: $300 per day (Inspectional Services Department).

unverifiable_exemptions: residences in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities
non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities

rules.title: H.3744 – Boston rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections home-rule petition
rules.requirement: A home-rule petition to let Boston adopt rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections was accompanied by a study order on 9/9/2024 and was not enacted. It gives Boston no rent stabilization authority.
rules.key_value: home-rule petition sent to study order (not enacted)
rules.quoted_span: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections

no_rule_findings.finding: The Boston rent stabilization home-rule petition H.3744 accompanied a study order and died, so no Boston rent stabilization authority exists through this bill.

dropped_candidates.reason: Folded into the no_rule_finding for rent_increase_limits (kept as the finding, same content).
Boston has the HSNA in force for just cause; the failed H.3744 is covered by the failed rent record. No separate just-cause finding.

parsed.notes: Boston documents support only the fair chance policy, fair housing/voucher rule, the HSNA, and the failed H.3744 petition. No Boston documents address security deposits, application fees, or algorithmic rent setting, so those categories are left empty without findings.
